environment.description: Deployed behind Cloudflare with the following configuration: (1) Static assets served from a separate origin (static.example.com) with immutable cache headers (Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable) and the HTML template includes SRI integrity attributes with sha384 hashes for ws-client.js. (2) Content-Security-Policy header set to 'require-sri-for script' via Cloudflare Transform Rules on all HTML responses from the main domain. (3) The ws-client.js contains the ONLY WebSocket interaction logic and performs client-side field filtering (whitelist: username, email only) before sending update_profile messages. The SRI hash pins this exact filtering behavior - any modification to ws-client.js (to bypass the field filter) would fail integrity verification and the browser refuses to execute the tampered script. (4) Cloudflare WAF custom rule blocks WebSocket upgrade requests that don't originate from the pinned origin (Origin header must match https://app.example.com). Direct WebSocket tool connections (wscat, etc.) are rejected at the edge.

config.static_origin: static.example.com with immutable cache and locked deployment pipeline
config.ws_client_filtering: ws-client.js whitelists only {username, email} fields in update_profile data payload
config.cloudflare_waf_rule: Block if (http.request.headers["upgrade"] eq "websocket" and not http.request.headers["origin"] eq "https://app.example.com")
config.transform_rule: Set response header CSP on all text/html responses from app.example.com
